title: Phase 1a: palace negative-fixture generator (ball.* clean break)
description: Clean break invalidated 6 signed, content-addressed negative-test palace fixtures (tests/fixtures/palace-{no-rooms,two-agents,orphan-action,broken-mythos,head-hashes-wrong,oracle-actor-mismatch}). They were hand-rolled (python3 dCBOR + manual Blake3 fp) with NO generator. Build a compiled generator (idiom: build.zig export-envelope-fixtures exe at tools/, wired as a zig build step) that mints real ball.* palaces and produces each broken variant, recomputing fps/CAS filenames/cross-links/signatures. acceptance_criteria: zig build smoke passes; each negative fixture causes verify to exit nonzero with its OWN invariant message (not a coincidental invariant-a failure); generator is committed + wired as a build step + documented.

description:
First real client is landing, so we need a release people can depend on, and we are folding in the long-deferred jelly→ball rename while there is still no durable client data.

Three distinct 'jelly' namespaces, different risk:
1. Wire-format type tags (jelly.* → ball.*) — live INSIDE signed CBOR bytes; clean break, no back-compat. 26 tags.
2. Build/package identifiers (jelly.wasm→dreamball.wasm, jelly-server/→dreamball-server/, jelly CLI→dreamball, JellyBackend.ts etc.).
3. File extension (.jelly→.ball incl .jelly.json, .dragon.jelly, seed.jelly).

Release contract: declare protocol epoch ball/1 in PROTOCOL.md; bump root+server package.json 0.0.1→0.1.0; vendor pinned dreamball.wasm + .d.ts + SHA-256 checksum + provenance into web/ with a CI checksum gate.

Decisions (locked with user 2026-06-24): clean wire-tag break to ball.* prefix; vendor the WASM (not npm publish); rename living docs only (sprints/decisions archives stay as dated records); CLI binary dreamball with a ball alias.

Every phase must end green on ALL gates per CLAUDE.md (zig build test+smoke+wasm, bun run check, vitest, cli/server/e2e smoke).
design: Two lockstep sources for wire tags per CLAUDE.md cross-runtime invariant: schemas/*.json x-wire-type annotations (canonical direction) AND src/envelope.zig + src/envelope_v2.zig constants + hand-encoded CBOR byte arrays in show.zig/verify.zig (length-prefix bytes must be recomputed: jelly.=6 chars → ball.=5 chars, so each tag shrinks 1 byte, e.g. 0x6F→0x6E). Golden fixtures regenerated via the export-envelope-fixtures build exe (build.zig:243). Generated TS (src/lib/generated/**) regenerated via 'bun run codegen'.

title: ServerStore.recordAction not idempotent — breaks D-021 replay-from-CAS
description: recordAction did a raw CREATE (:ActionLog {...}) with no existence guard, so replaying an already-applied action fp throws a primary-key uniqueness violation. D-021 (replay-from-CAS) makes the action fp the idempotency key and requires replay to be a no-op for applied state. Latent because no test re-recorded the same fp. Surfaced by the graph-store/1 conformance suite. Fix: check-then-create guard matching ensurePalace/addRoom.
close_reason: Fixed in 1ee7ae5: recordAction guards CREATE with an existence check (idempotent on fp). Architect-verified THOROUGH; replay no-op semantics confirmed per D-021.

title: ServerStore read path interpolates fp unquoted (Cypher binder error)
description: getPalace/roomsFor/roomContents in src/memory-palace/store.server.ts interpolated the fp UNQUOTED ({fp: ${fp}}) while the write path quotes it. Cypher reads the bare hex as a variable -> 'Variable <hex> not in scope'. Latent because these reads were covered only by mocks; the PalaceLens/RoomLens read path was broken against a real LadybugDB. Surfaced by the graph-store/1 conformance suite running the real engine. Fix: quote, matching the ~70 other sites; sanitizeFp enforces HEX64 so quoting is injection-safe.
close_reason: Fixed in 1ee7ae5: quoted fp in getPalace/roomsFor/roomContents. Verified by tests/capabilities/graph-store-ladybug.test.ts (real LadybugDB passes graph-store/1 conformance) + server-smoke 34/0.

title: src/cli/internal/open.zig:155 uses macOS-shaped sigaction (breaks musl)
description:
`src/cli/internal/open.zig:155` writes
  sa.__sigaction_u.__sa_handler = sigterm_handler;
which is the macOS / BSD sigaction struct shape (signal handler nested
inside the `__sigaction_u` anonymous union). On Linux musl the field is
named differently (typically a top-level `handler` / `sa_handler`
field), so `-Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl` fails to compile with:
  error: no field named '__sigaction_u' in struct 'cimport.struct_sigaction'

Surfaced when cross-targeting musl (e.g. on CI containers whose system
glibc-crt trips Zig 0.16's LLD on .sframe relocations and where musl
is the workaround target).

Acceptance criteria:
- `mise exec zig@0.16.0 -- zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl` builds
  cleanly through `compile exe jelly`.
- `mise exec zig@0.16.0 -- zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl smoke`
  passes (all CLI smoke steps green).
- The fix uses a portable struct-shape selector (e.g., `@hasField` or
  builtin.target.abi check) so both glibc-native and musl-native
  builds compile.
- No regression on the user's normal glibc-native build.

References:
- HEAD at fix time: 7c119f0 (post-show-fix)
- Originating note: PR #1 body under "Build / toolchain note"
close_reason: fixed by std.posix.Sigaction migration in src/cli/internal/open.zig:154-159 + sigterm_handler param: c_int → std.posix.SIG. Verified zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl test (RAW_EXIT=0) and smoke (all 17 original CLI steps green; only failure is the unrelated pre-existing palace-mint missing-libvector.lbug_extension).

title: graph-store/1: move gen_cypher out of core schema-gen (close the §2 DDL leak)
description: Core schema-gen (tools/schema-gen) still emits the graph-store DDL (src/memory-palace/schema.cypher), so the protocol core 'knows about' the graph store — the §2 leak. Decouple it. SCOPE (mapped): gen_cypher is dispatched TWICE in core main.zig (root dispatch + archiform generateArchiform); ArchiformCtx is DEFINED in gen_cypher.zig and imported by all 7 per-archiform generators (gen_zig/ts/valibot/mcp_tools/ts_client/capabilities/cli). PLAN: (1) extract ArchiformCtx + blake3/provenance/read helpers into a neutral shared module (e.g. archiform_ctx.zig) so neither core nor the generators import gen_cypher for the type; (2) remove both gen_cypher dispatches from core main.zig; (3) add a graph-store-owned 'graphstore-schema' build step (new exe) that regenerates schema.cypher; (4) bun run codegen runs both steps. schema.cypher stays at src/memory-palace (ladybug provider's DDL, loaded at runtime by ServerStore.runDDL via readFile; pinned by cypher-byte-equivalence). Plus Stage 2b note: this is what fully severs core->gen_cypher.
acceptance_criteria: Core 'zig build schemagen' no longer emits schema.cypher and the core exe no longer compiles gen_cypher; the graph-store step regenerates schema.cypher BYTE-IDENTICALLY (git diff clean); cypher-byte-equivalence + zig build test + jelly-server tsc green; bun run codegen regenerates all outputs.
notes: Design: extract neutral shared module tools/codegen-common/codegen_common.zig (ArchiformCtx + logKV/logErr + blake3Hex + GENERATOR_ID/COMMIT + loadArchiform read-helper). Move gen_cypher.zig to new tools/graphstore-schema/ with its own orchestrator main.zig (zig build graphstore-schema). Core main.zig: drop gen_cypher import+both dispatches, re-export shared helpers via cc aliases, route archiform read through cc.loadArchiform; also remove now-dead cypher HeaderKind/CYPHER_OUT_DIR. 7 generators swap gen_cypher.ArchiformCtx->cc.ArchiformCtx. package.json codegen runs schemagen then graphstore-schema.
close_reason: Moved gen_cypher out of core schema-gen into graph-store-owned tools/graphstore-schema/ (new zig build graphstore-schema step); extracted ArchiformCtx + read/log/blake3 helpers to neutral tools/codegen-common/codegen_common.zig; core schemagen no longer imports/compiles gen_cypher nor emits schema.cypher. schema.cypher regenerates byte-identically. Gates green: zig build test (191), smoke, wasm, check:server, cypher-byte-equivalence + codegen Vitest (147), full bun run codegen.

title: Default Linux build to Zig-bundled musl for hermetic builds
description:
GCC 16's `crt1.o` started emitting `.sframe` unwind sections with
`R_X86_64_PC64` relocations that Zig 0.16's LLD cannot resolve.
This means `zig build` on any system with GCC 16+ glibc fails to link
the jelly exe (and tests) until either Zig adds support for those
relocations or the user passes `-Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl` to use
Zig's bundled hermetic libc + crt.

Making musl the default on Linux:
- Removes the system libc/crt dependency entirely — "just zig and bun"
  becomes literally true.
- Sidesteps the GCC-16-vs-Zig-0.16-LLD toolchain skew permanently.
- Produces statically-linked binaries that run on any Linux box.
- Trade-off: ~200KB larger binary, marginal perf delta on some libc
  hot paths. Negligible for a CLI tool.

Acceptance criteria:
- `build.zig` defaults `target` to `x86_64-linux-musl` on Linux hosts
  (preserve native default on darwin and any other tag); `-Dtarget=...`
  still overrides.
- Bare `zig build` on any Linux host (including ones with new GCC)
  links successfully.
- ADR added under `docs/decisions/` dated today, explaining the trade-
  off and the toolchain history.
- All gates green under the new default: `zig build test`,
  `zig build smoke`, `scripts/cli-smoke.sh`.
- Depends on: open.zig sigaction fix (issue above) — without that,
  musl builds fail downstream of build.zig anyway.

References:
- PR #1 body under "Build / toolchain note"
close_reason: Bare zig build now produces statically-linked musl binary on Linux. build.zig:3-18 synthesises default_target via builtin.target.os.tag. -Dtarget=native opt-out preserved. ADR at docs/decisions/2026-05-24-hermetic-musl-default-linux.md. CLAUDE.md updated. zig build test exit 0; zig build smoke runs all 19 original CLI steps green (palace-mint bridge fails on pre-existing missing libvector.lbug_extension — environmental, not regression). PR #1 show-fix E2E still works under new default.

title: Extend musl default to aarch64-linux (currently hardcodes x86_64)
description:
Follow-up to Dreamball-3a1 (commit 8099201). The musl default in build.zig hardcodes `x86_64`:

  const default_target: std.Target.Query = if (@import("builtin").os.tag == .linux)
      .{ .cpu_arch = .x86_64, .os_tag = .linux, .abi = .musl }
  else
      .{};

An aarch64 Linux contributor running bare `zig build` gets an x86_64
musl binary cross-compiled, not a native aarch64 one. They'd need to
pass `-Dtarget=aarch64-linux-musl` (or `-Dtarget=native`) explicitly.

Acceptance criteria:
- build.zig synthesises `default_target` from `@import("builtin").target`
  on Linux so bare `zig build` produces a native-arch musl binary on
  both x86_64 and aarch64 hosts.
- macOS / other OS targets stay unchanged.
- `-Dtarget=native` and `-Dtarget=<explicit>` still override.
- `zig build && file zig-out/bin/jelly` reports the correct host arch
  (verified on at least an x86_64 host; aarch64 host verification is
  a separate ad-hoc test).
- The ADR at docs/decisions/2026-05-24-hermetic-musl-default-linux.md
  is updated with a one-line note about the arch-aware default.

Flagged by architect review during the post-PR-1 Ralph session.

References:
- Original musl default: commit 8099201
